title: Evaluation of online support: Online cognitive behavioral therapy for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD NET program)
summary: The current situation during the COVID-19 pandemic presents the psychiatric outpatient clinic of the Leipzig University Hospital with the challenge of maintaining adequate psychiatric and psychosocial care for psychiatric outpatients despite the present governmental restrictions due to the pandemic. Many outpatients who were attending the therapeutic and group sessions in the outpatient clinic regularly several times a week are not able to do so in the current situation. As a consequence, these patients do not get the necessary therapeutic support and the missing clinic appointments negatively affect their daily structure. This study aims to provide a guided online intervention (program based on cognitive behavioral therapy) for patients of the psychiatric outpatient clinic with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD NET program). The aim of this study is to examine the feasibility and acceptance of the OCD NET program and evaluate its effect on the patients’ symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder and their quality of life. Within an ongoing evaluation of the feasibility and acceptance of the OCD NET program and its effect on the patients’ symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder and their quality of life, data collection is ongoing beyond the initial sample size of N = 40.

interventions.name: Study participants (patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder, age 18 or over) will be offered to participate in the therapist-guided online program OCD NET over the course of 10 weeks.
